claims.text: The protective coating has a mixed FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy microstructure.
The coating's creep resistance under continuous loading is governed by optimization of its microstructure and composition.
Microstructure and composition optimization reduces progressive plastic deformation.
Adding alloying elements such as Ti or Nb and adjusting processing temperature and time can refine grain size and modify phase distribution.
The proposed optimization increases lattice friction stress.
The proposed optimization promotes a more stable dislocation network.
Increased lattice friction stress hinders dislocation movement.
Hindered dislocation movement reduces progressive plastic deformation and improves creep resistance.
At 600 °C and 200 MPa, the optimized coating is predicted to have a minimum creep rate of 7.0 × 10^-5 s^-1 rather than the baseline value of 1.0 × 10^-4 s^-1.
The predicted minimum-creep-rate reduction relative to the baseline is 30%.
The baseline coating is as-cast, coarse-grained, and has a mixed FCC/BCC microstructure.
The proposed optimization is effective from 500 °C to 700 °C and from 150 MPa to 250 MPa.
The optimized and baseline coatings should be compared under identical loading conditions using minimum creep rate, microstructure, and dislocation density and distribution as measurements.
Failure to reduce the minimum creep rate by at least 20% relative to the baseline under the same loading conditions falsifies the hypothesis.
